Timeline API Reference¶

Back to PlussQit API Reference

This page documents pluss::Timeline one method at a time. Each method page is handwritten, navigable from the sidebar, and backed by compiled examples whose displayed output comes from the implementation.

What Timeline Is¶

Timeline is the general temporal payload object in PlussQit.

Use it when timestamps are part of the data itself:

  • a scalar moment

  • a 1D column of event times

  • a 2D or 3D temporal tensor

  • date-part extraction

  • text formatting of timestamps

  • timezone conversion

  • mask-based filling and temporal selection

Use TimeIndex instead when the timestamps are the ordered case axis and you specifically want ordered lookup, as-of matching, resampling, rolling windows, and alignment semantics.

That difference is the clean split:

  • Timeline is the general time payload.

  • TimeIndex is the 1D ordered time axis surface built on top of a Timeline.

Includes¶

#include <pluss/pluss.h>

Practical Construction Patterns¶

Example 1. Build a scalar timestamp.

auto t = pluss::timeline::make("2026-03-14T09:26:53Z");

Example 2. Build a 1D temporal vector.

auto t = pluss::timeline::make({
    "2026-03-14T09:00:00Z",
    "2026-03-14T10:00:00Z",
    "2026-03-14T11:00:00Z",
});

Example 3. Build a higher-rank temporal array.

auto t = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2026-03-14T09:00:00Z", "2026-03-14T10:00:00Z"},
    {"2026-03-15T09:00:00Z", "2026-03-15T10:00:00Z"},
});

Example 4. Build directly from raw epoch nanoseconds.

auto t = pluss::timeline::from_epoch({
    1'773'484'800'000'000'000LL,
    1'773'488'400'000'000'000LL,
});

Reading ISO-like Timestamps¶

Pluss accepts ISO-8601-style timestamp text, so you will often see forms like:

2026-03-14T09:26:53Z

  • T Separates the date portion from the time portion.

  • Z Means UTC, also called Zulu time.

Other common forms are also valid when the parser can unambiguously interpret them:

  • 2026-03-14T09:26:53+00:00 UTC written as an explicit numeric offset.

  • 2026-03-14T09:26:53-07:00 A timestamp with a negative timezone offset.

  • 2026-03-14 A date-only form, usually interpreted as midnight on that date.

Important current behavior:

  • The documented text path for an absent instant is an empty string, not the literal text "NaT".

  • Timeline may contain absent instants, and those render as NaT.

Coverage¶

The current handwritten pages cover these starting families:

  • representation and export: defined, sizes, dim, numel, is_scalar, tz, host, from_buffer, ticks, copy_ticks, and the shape-preserving epoch_* projections

  • component and coarse-epoch construction: from_ymd, from_ymdhms, from_epoch_micros, from_epoch_millis, from_epoch_seconds

  • temporal operators, arithmetic, and distance: operators, calendar-aware add_years, add_months, and add_days, fixed elapsed add_hours, add_minutes, add_seconds, and add_nanos, plus add_duration, sub_duration, exact diff, policy-driven integer span, scalar calendar years_between and months_between, and scalar elapsed days_between, hours_between, minutes_between, and seconds_between

  • elementwise comparisons: eq, ne, lt, le, gt, ge

  • validity and absent-instant handling: isnat, isvalid, isnat_scalar, fill_nat, where

  • temporal ordering and identity: argsort, min, max, sort, unique

  • structural axis-0 operations: concat, repeat, empty_like, and shape-preserving constant construction with fill_like

  • runtime-selected temporal movement with shift, and checked promotion from a one-dimensional Timeline to TimeIndex with to_timeindex

  • scalar formatting: isoformat

  • formatting and text conversion: strftime, to_note_iso, weekday_name, and month_name; custom layouts belong in strftime() rather than named formatting aliases

  • rounding and projection: floor, ceil, round, date, time, and local calendar boundary projection with period_start

  • timezone work: tz_convert, tz_localize

  • ordered insertion helpers on sorted 1D timelines: searchsorted_left, searchsorted_right

  • calendar component extraction: year, month, day, hour, minute, second, nanosecond, microsecond, millisecond, weekday, dayofyear, quarter, week, plus native-value scalar extraction through year_scalar, month_scalar, day_scalar, hour_scalar, minute_scalar, second_scalar, quarter_scalar, week_scalar, weekday_scalar, and yearday_scalar

  • scalar calendar predicates: leap_scalar, month_start_scalar, month_end_scalar, quarter_start_scalar, quarter_end_scalar, and is_weekend_scalar

  • strict local-calendar field replacement: set_year, set_month, set_day, set_hour, set_minute, set_second

  • calendar predicates: is_leap_year, boundary predicates, business-day predicates, and the weekday-specific predicates

  • regular sequence construction: date_range(...)

This is not yet the full public surface. The representation, export, ordering, canonical calendar-field, calendar-shift, elapsed-shift, and calendar-predicate layers are documented method by method. The Timeline reference documents one canonical spelling for each operation rather than carrying compatibility aliases.
